methodological_rigor.justification: This is a three-arm case-control study with 35 men per group, BMI-matched, with an a priori power calculation (80%, alpha 0.05) via G*Power. Analyses appropriately separated Gaussian vs non-Gaussian variables (Shapiro-Wilk, ANOVA/ANCOVA on log-transformed data, Kruskal-Wallis with GLM Tweedie), adjusted for age and BMI, and used Tukey-Kramer correction for pairwise post hoc tests. However, ELISA inter-assay CV was very high (up to 25.54% for Apo CIII), samples were recruited across an 11-year window (2010-2021), fasting status was unknown for the mPCa group, and all mPCa patients received ADT, which authors acknowledge as a major confounder that cannot be disentangled from metastatic status. No correction for multiplicity across the many correlation comparisons in Figure 3 was described, and effect sizes/CIs for group comparisons are not reported (only means +/- SD and p-values).

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Design is an individual case-control comparison of three convenience-sampled groups from two biobanks, which maps to Oxford LoE 3b. Translational relevance is plausible because drugs against ANGPTL3 (evinacumab), Apo CIII (volanesorsen, olezarsen, plozasiran) and PCSK9 (evolocumab) already exist and the authors suggest repurposing, but the study is associative and cannot establish causality or mechanism in PCa. The findings could motivate biomarker validation or early-phase repositioning trials, but the confound of universal ADT in the mPCa arm and small sample prevent near-term practice impact.

reporting_quality.justification: As a case-control observational study, STROBE applies. The manuscript reports eligibility criteria, biobank sources, ethics approvals, sample handling, assay details (catalog numbers, intra/inter-assay CVs), covariate adjustments and statistical software versions, which covers many STROBE items. However, STROBE is not explicitly cited, a flow diagram of participant selection is absent, missing-data handling is not described (beyond Lp(a) imputation at half LOD), and there is no statement on data/code sharing within the excerpted text. Reproducibility is limited because individual-level data availability and analysis code are not mentioned.

novelty_literature.justification: The authors frame this as the first simultaneous profiling of circulating Apo CIII, ANGPTL3, leptin, PCSK9 and Lp(a) across metastatic, localized Gleason 8/9 and at-risk controls, which is a meaningful combination. Individual associations of leptin, PCSK9, ANGPTL3 and lipids with PCa have been reported previously (extensively cited in the manuscript itself). The paradoxical negative PCSK9-LDL correlation in the pooled cohort adds a novel descriptive observation, but the work is a focused extension of known hyperlipidemic-factor biology rather than a mechanistic or first-in-class discovery.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is clearly organized with logical IMRaD structure, detailed methods, and a thorough discussion that contextualizes each analyte (triglycerides, ANGPTL3, Apo CIII, leptin, PCSK9, Lp(a), LPL, ADT). Numerical results are reported with means, SDs and p-values consistently in-text and in Table 1, and a dedicated Limitations subsection openly addresses sample size, ELISA variability, BMI as a body-composition proxy, sarcopenia and unknown fasting status. Some sections (e.g., 4.3 LPL, 4.5 PCSK9) are dense and would benefit from tightening, and figures/tables could not be visually evaluated from the text-only version, but prose is precise and grammatically clean.

key_strengths: A priori power calculation (G*Power, 80% power, alpha 0.05) and BMI-matched three-arm design comparing at-risk, localized Gleason 8/9 and metastatic PCa.

Appropriate analytic choices: Shapiro-Wilk, ANCOVA on log-transformed Gaussian variables, Tweedie GLM for skewed analytes, partial Spearman correlations adjusted for age and BMI, plus Tukey-Kramer multiplicity correction for pairwise comparisons.
Clear translational framing tied to existing approved/late-stage lipid-lowering drugs (evinacumab, volanesorsen, olezarsen, plozasiran, evolocumab).
Transparent, self-critical Limitations section addressing ELISA CVs, ADT confounding, unknown fasting status in mPCa, and the inadequacy of BMI as a body-composition surrogate.
key_concerns: Universal ADT exposure in the mPCa arm confounds the core finding; authors themselves acknowledge ADT can raise triglycerides up to 25% and cholesterol up to 10%, so metastasis-specific effects cannot be isolated.
ELISA inter-assay CV reached 25.54% for Apo CIII and 16.90% for ANGPTL3, which could drive or inflate the modest between-group differences.

Small sample (n=35/group), 11-year sample accrual window (2010-2021), unknown fasting status in the metastatic group, and no described handling of multiplicity across the extensive correlation matrices.
LoE 3b case-control evidence with no independent validation cohort; findings are associative and do not establish causality or clinical utility.
Reporting standard (STROBE) not explicitly followed, no participant flow diagram, no data/code availability statement visible in the extracted text.
chief_reviewer.rationale: Methodologically competent but modest hypothesis-generating case-control study with honest limitations; the universal ADT confound, small n and high ELISA variability cap its impact, placing it at tier 3 (journals like Cancers or BMC Cancer) with minor revisions rather than tier 2.
